title: Lemon Pepper Wings
subtitle: Crisp oven wings with a dry lemon-pepper rub
excerpt: Lemon pepper wings are baked until very crisp then tossed in lemon zest, butter, coarsely ground black pepper, and salt. Unlike buffalo and honey garlic wings, they're dressed with dry seasoning rather than a wet sauce, so the skin stays crisp.
sourceNotes: Lemon pepper wings became popular in American bars and restaurants, particularly in Atlanta, Georgia, in the 1990s and 2000s. The dry-seasoned style is distinct from wet-sauce wing traditions.

recipe.batchNotes: Scale easily: use two oven trays and rotate them halfway through.

content.text: Lemon pepper wings are baked at high heat until really crisp, then tossed in melted butter, lemon zest, and plenty of black pepper. The zest is the flavour and the butter is the carrier: fresh lemon zest works far better than the commercial lemon pepper seasoning sold in jars. The wings stay crispier than wet-sauced wings because the coating is mostly dry.

items.prepNote: tips removed, split at the joint
zest of both, juice of one

content.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (fan 200°C / gas mark 7). Pat {{chicken-wings}} completely dry. Toss in {{rapeseed-oil}}, {{sea-salt-flakes}}, and {{baking-powder}} if using (the baking powder helps the skin crisp). Arrange on a rack over a lined baking tray, skin side up.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes, turning once halfway through, until the skin is golden and really crisp. The wings should be slightly mahogany-coloured, not pale gold.
Melt {{unsalted-butter}} in a small pan. Add the zest of both {{lemon}}, the juice of one, {{black-pepper}}, {{sea-salt-flakes}}, and {{garlic-powder}}. Stir to combine and remove from the heat.
Toss the hot wings in the lemon butter mixture immediately out of the oven. The coating should be light: you want every wing glossy with zest and butter, not dripping. Serve straight away.

items.cause: Wings not dry before cooking, or baking powder omitted.
items.fix: The baking powder is the key trick: it raises the pH of the skin and promotes crispness. Make sure the wings are as dry as possible. A rack is essential.

items.cause: Lemon zest quantity was too small, or the zest was added too early.
items.fix: Zest generously and add it off the heat: heat destroys the volatile compounds that give lemon its bright flavour. Use the zest of two lemons, not one.

items.symptom: The wings lose their crispness quickly after tossing
items.cause: Butter coating makes the skin steam slightly.
items.fix: Use only enough butter to coat lightly. Serve within five minutes of tossing.

items.symptom: The pepper is too harsh and overpowering
items.cause: Freshly and coarsely ground black pepper can be very assertive.
items.fix: Start with one teaspoon and taste before adding the second. Coarsely ground pepper is milder than finely ground. The lemon should balance the pepper: if the pepper dominates, add more zest.

content.text: Lemon pepper wings are linked to Atlanta, Georgia, where they became a city-wide favourite from the 1990s and feature across the bar and restaurant scene. The style is now national, but Atlanta's claim to it as a local signature is well established. The dry seasoning approach makes them good eating for people who find wet-sauced wings messy.
